stories.title: Building wealth is only half the battle Prosper
stories.excerpt: An aerial photo of Kampala city. Diversification can spread risk, but it does not on its own guarantee that wealth will survive its founder. PHOTO/ MICHAEL…
stories.summary: The discussion moved beyond earning money to the risks of concentrating assets, weak governance, poor planning and the difficulty of transferring wealth from one generation to another. Mr Kasolo describes the wealth journey in four stages: creation, growth, preservation and transfer. By March 2026, the Authority reported that retirement assets had reached Shs35.6 trillion.

stories.title: The changing customer Prosper
stories.excerpt: An employee communicates with a customer. Phone support allows for more personalised interactions with customers. PHOTO/ MICHAEL KAKUMIRIZI
stories.summary: An employee communicates with a customer. Price to payAccording to industry analysts, there is a price to pay for poor customer service and experience. Dr Dorothy Kyeyune, a thought leader in leadership, customer experience, and organisational strategy, notes that assessing service quality in Uganda requires first distinguishing between Customer Service (CS) and Customer Experience (CX).“Customer service is a single, specific interaction when a customer needs help or encounters a problem,” Dr Kyeyune explained.
